question: A new investigation by Lighthouse Reports, Evident and Sudan War Monitor has found that Rapid Support Forces (RSF) fighters are being trained in Libyan camps by the Libyan National Army and mercenaries contracted by the United Arab Emirates (UAE), using UAEsupplied weapons.
These findings come as the UN Security Council warns of an imminent risk of mass atrocities in El Obeid, and as the EU prepares its next round of trade negotiations with the UAE.

MEPs have questioned whether concluding such an agreement with a state accused of prolonging a conflict involving serious crimes under international law is compatible with the EU’s obligations under Article 21 of the Treaty on European Union (TEU). In light of the above: 1.

Does the Commission consider the continuation of EU-UAE trade negotiations to be compatible with Article 21 TEU and the EU’s commitments on atrocity prevention and arms-export control, given mounting evidence of UAE support to the RSF?

Will the Commission propose suspending EU-UAE trade negotiations until allegations of UAE support to the RSF and other actors implicated in atrocity crimes in Sudan are clarified, including via independent investigation and cooperation with UN mechanisms?

What steps is the Commission taking to ensure that any future EU-UAE trade agreement is conditional on the UAE ending all military, logistical or financial support to parties in Sudan’s conflict, and on full compliance with the Darfur arms embargo and international humanitarian law?
